plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked cone-wavelength sensitivity and X-linked prevalence chart from Young (1802), Helmholtz (1852), and Hunt & Mollon (17 February 1995 Science 267: 984–988) shows S-cones (420 nm), M-cones (534 nm, absent in John Dalton's deuteranopia), and L-cones (564 nm) combining to distinguish ~1,000,000 hues, and contrasts male (~8% = 1 in 12) vs female (~0.5% = 1 in 200) red-green colour blindness.

teach_overlay.scale: because each of your three cone types can distinguish about one hundred steps of brightness, three cones multiplying one hundred by one hundred by one hundred let your brain see roughly one million different shades
